To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) SimpleDB is a good candidate for the storage of small RDF data items; 2) the use of a key-value store for RDF data management requires an appropriate indexing strategy; and 3) our indexing strategies provide a good trade-off between the quality of the results (precision and recall) and the query response time.

1) the use of AWS for RDF data management is feasible; 2) the performance of AWS can be significantly improved by using the right indexing strategy; and 3) the performance of an RDF data management system can be significantly improved when the data are distributed across multiple cloud providers

(1) the SimpleDB service can be used as a scalable and fault-tolerant storage system for RDF data, (2) it is possible to build a scalable RDF query processor on top of SimpleDB, (3) it is possible, by using Simple DB, to build an efficient and scalable RDF index for the identification of relevant RDF datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to efficiently and effectively store and index RDF data in the cloud.
the problem of how to efficiently index RDF data in a commercial cloud infrastructure, and how to route RDF queries to the appropriate data sources.
the following question: how to exploit a commercial cloud infrastructure, such as AWS, for distributed RDF data management?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of AWS for managing RDF data is a promising research direction, but that there is a need to further develop and evaluate more sophisticated indexing and query processing strategies.
the proposed architecture is a good starting point, but there are still a number of open issues to be addressed in future work.
the proposed indexing techniques are effective in terms of query processing time, but the performance of the index construction process is still an open issue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although SimpleDB does not provide any native support for RDF data management, we can still use it for indexing RDF datasets in a distributed manner, with reasonable efficiency.
, although the cloud infrastructure can be used as a scalable platform for RDF data management, it is still not mature enough for the task, especially in terms of performance and cost.
we have shown how to build a scalable and efficient RDF data management system in the cloud.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the cloud is not yet a viable solution for RDF data management, it is a promising one.
the use of a cloud infrastructure can significantly reduce the costs of storing RDF data and managing RDF data access.

, while AWS provides a powerful infrastructure for the deployment of distributed RDF data management applications, the performance of these applications is highly dependent on how well the data is organized and partitioned among the nodes of the cloud.
